messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The test `testEncoder()` fails because it compares the output of the `Base64.encode()` instance method to a precomputed UTF-8 byte array. The current bug report indicates that in Commons Codec 1.4, the instance method `Base64.encode()` appends CRLF sequences and chunks the output into 76-character lines, unlike version 1.3, which did not do this. This results in the output containing additional newline characters that cause the comparison with the expected byte array to fail.

Examining the `Base64.encode(byte[])` method (lines 928-950), the method calculates the output length based on the line length and line separator settings by calling the `getEncodeLength()` method. Then it encodes the input bytes in chunks, potentially adding line separators.

The `getEncodeLength()` method (lines 963-980) shows that if chunking is enabled (line length > 0), the length calculation includes the length of the line separators (e.g., CRLF), adding these between chunks.

In the `encode(byte[], int, int)` method (lines 452-513), when encoding the final bytes (`inAvail < 0`), if `lineLength > 0` and some data is present (`pos > 0`), it appends the line separator (e.g., CRLF) at the end (lines 484-487). Additionally, during encoding, after exactly 76 characters have been output (controlled by `lineLength` and `currentLinePos`), it appends the line separator (lines 505-509).

Constructor analysis:
The no-arg constructor `Base64()` (lines 224-226) calls `this(false)`.
The constructor `Base64(boolean urlSafe)` (lines 243-246) calls `this(CHUNK_SIZE, CHUNK_SEPARATOR, urlSafe)`.
The main constructor `Base64(int lineLength, byte[] lineSeparator, boolean urlSafe)` (lines 320-339) sets the `lineLength`, `lineSeparator`, and `encodeSize` fields. It keeps the default `lineLength` as `CHUNK_SIZE` (most likely 76) and default `lineSeparator` as `CRLF` (likely \r\n). This means by default the instance encoder will chunk encoded Base64 strings into 76-character lines and separate them with CRLF.

Because the test instantiates `new Base64()` without parameters, it uses the default chunking behavior, causing the encoded output to have CRLF line separators every 76 characters. This differs from the static `Base64.encodeBase64()` method which does not chunk by default and does not add trailing CRLF, explaining the test failure and discrepancy with version 1.3 where chunking was not enabled by default.

In summary, the root cause of the failure is that the instance method `Base64.encode()` now adds chunking and trailing CRLF line separators by default, breaking tests expecting continuous output without line breaks.

No relevant recent bug reports appear related and do not affect this diagnosis.

The fix should focus on the `Base64` constructor behavior, changing the default `lineLength` or exposing a way to disable chunking / trailing line separator when calling `encode()`. Alternatively, adjust the `encode()` method to optionally suppress trailing line separators if chunking is enabled.

This matches the test failure and current bug report's description.
